central_question: Conjecture 9.2 (arXiv:2304.04690 §9): a loopless digraph (digons allowed, no parallel arcs) is 2-EXTREMAL iff it lies in H_2. D is k-extremal iff it is strong, underlying-2-connected, and chi_vec(D)=lambda(D)+1=k+1; 2-extremal means lambda(D)=2 and chi_vec(D)=3 (and D is Eulerian, in=out>=2, (k+1)-dicritical by AAC Lemma 4.1). H_2 = smallest digraph class containing all SYMMETRIC ODD CYCLES, closed under the DIRECTED HAJOS JOIN (Def 1.5) and the 2-HAJOS TREE JOIN (Def 9.1, even-leaf-path B-parity). The paper proves the easy inclusion H_2 subset 2-extremal; the open direction is 2-extremal => H_2.

proved.claim: No 2-extremal digraph has a 2-arc-cut digon (a digon cannot be the only x-y connection in a strong underlying-2-connected digraph; Menger). Hence the induction seam CANNOT be a single cut digon; Def-9.1 clause (b) must be the general tree-join sense.
In a 2-extremal digraph the DIGON GRAPH F_D is always a forest, and the single arcs are in/out balanced (decompose into closed directed trails).

DIRECTED-HAJOS half of Conditional L = BJSS Theorem 2 (arXiv:1908.04096): for D=D1 (directed Hajos join) D2, chi_vec(D)>=min(chi_vec(D1),chi_vec(D2)); the 5-line cross-seam splice C1∪C2 - u1v1 - v2u2 + u1u2. KNOWN THEOREM, cited-verified vs primary PDF, splice independently survived. Closes the directed-Hajos sub-instance of the colouring half — but NOT the tree-join half, NOT Lemma A, NOT Conj 9.2.

MIXED-2-CUT NECESSITY: a directed-Hajos merge vertex forces MC(D)=1; contrapositive MC(D)=0 => no Hajos seam (so the 3 tree-join-only n=7 members are provably clause-(b)-only). 3-connected => MC=0. Constrains seam TYPE only, never seam EXISTENCE.

H_2 => U(D) PLANAR (the planarity angle): every H_2 member has planar underlying graph; and 2-sum preserves planarity, 3-connected 2-extremal => generalised wheel (base, strongly supported). So a NON-PLANAR 2-extremal digraph would DISPROVE Conj 9.2.

CUT IDENTITY: for an Eulerian digraph D (digons F_D + balanced single arcs), every vertex cut S satisfies arcs(S->S̄) = (d_S + |E_U(S)|)/2 (d_S = digons crossing); hence lambda_D(u,v) = min_{S sep u,v} (d_S+|E_U(S)|)/2, and d_S+|E_U(S)| is EVEN.

From T1: lambda_D(u,v) >= lambda'_U(u,v)/2, so 2-extremal => MAX LOCAL edge-connectivity lambda'(U) <= 4 (no pair has >=5 edge-disjoint paths; verified all 52 truth-set). For a 3-CONNECTED 2-extremal D: uniform lambda_D(u,v)=2 for EVERY pair, and each digon edge's tight separating cut has type (1,3) (crosses that digon + exactly 2 single edges). M-MULTIGRAPH REFORMULATION: doubling digons / single-arc=1 edge gives M with lambda_M=2 lambda_D, so 3-conn 2-extremal => M is UNIFORMLY 4-EDGE-CONNECTED.

CONDITIONAL STRUCTURAL LEMMA (Steps 2-4): if D is 3-connected 2-extremal AND F_D is a SPANNING TREE, then the single arcs form ONE directed cycle on exactly the leaves of F_D in plane order with even leaf-parity => D is a generalised wheel. So '3-connected 2-extremal => generalised wheel' is PROVED MODULO Step 1 (F_D is a spanning tree) alone. Step 1 <=> 'no digon-free cut' <=> exclude k(F_D)>=2 components.

graveyard.claim: DIGRAPH GALLAI-DIRAC SEPARATOR reduction (literature, Harutyunyan-Mohar 2011 / BJSS Thm 15): in a 3-dicritical digraph the separating interface of a disconnected F_D must be a Gallai-tree obstruction not a plain forest, forcing a size-2 separator (MC=1) incompatible with 3-connectivity => 3-conn + chi=3 => F_D connected for all k.

It makes NO claim about vertex separators, cut sets, or separating interfaces, and does NOT forbid a forest-inducing separator in a dicritical digraph. The central inference ('separating interface must be a Gallai-tree obstruction') is a FABRICATED specialisation conflating D_low with a separator interface; the classical Dirac-Gallai motivation is likewise misstated. Independently the grounding is VACUOUS w.r.t. the reduction (G9/G15 class): truth set L3..L7 has every k>=2 member at kappa=2 (3-conn antecedent empty there) and the 'generic census' found 72 three-conn lambda=2 k>=2 members ALL chi=2 (zero chi=3 antecedent), reproducing D4's existing empirics without ever exercising the Gallai inference.
